definitions.gloss: kun reading; reading a kanji using its native Japanese meaning; reading classical Chinese texts in Japanese word order
definitions.explanation: Reading kanji with the native Japanese word that matches the character's meaning, as opposed to the on'yomi (Sino-Japanese reading). Also refers to the practice of reading classical Chinese texts with Japanese word order.

examples.english: The kun reading of 山 is 'yama.'

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{訓読|くんよ}み⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{音読|おんよ}み→音読み：10453_onyomi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: This kanji changes meaning depending on the kun or on reading.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{訓読|くんどく}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{方法|ほうほう}→方法：03621_houhou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{古典|こてん}→古典：00242_koten⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: The method of reading classical Chinese in Japanese word order is taught in high school classics class.

notes:
USAGE:
In everyday kanji study, {訓読|くんよ}み (kun'yomi) refers to the native Japanese reading of a kanji character, while ⟦{音読|おんよ}み→音読み：10453_onyomi⟧ (on'yomi) is the Sino-Japanese reading. In classical studies, {訓読|くんどく} also refers to the technique of rearranging classical Chinese (⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧) into Japanese word order for reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {訓読|くんよ}み⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to read using kun reading)
- {訓読|くんよ}み (kun reading — the more common everyday form)
- ⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{訓読|くんどく} (reading classical Chinese in Japanese)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{音読|おんよ}み→音読み：10453_onyomi⟧: on'yomi — the Sino-Japanese reading of a kanji character
- {訓|くん}: kun — shortened form often used in dictionaries for the native reading
